hazards.mechanism: Middleware parses, decompresses, decodes, or reserializes the body before signature verification.
hazards.evidence: Trace bytes from the socket through proxy and framework middleware to the verifier, including content encoding and body limits.
hazards.control: Capture the exact signed representation and call the provider verifier before parsing or side effects.
hazards.detection: Measure verification failures after deployments by route, content type, and middleware version.
hazards.recovery: Restore raw-body handling, rotate a secret only if exposure occurred, and replay provider-retained events safely.
hazards.test: Show that whitespace, key order, Unicode normalization, and decompression changes fail verification.

hazards.mechanism: A correctly signed delivery is replayed inside the timestamp tolerance and repeats a financial or fulfillment effect.
hazards.evidence: Inspect signed timestamp policy, durable event identity, semantic effect keys, and replay-tool behavior.
hazards.control: Combine bounded timestamp tolerance with durable delivery dedupe and idempotency at every downstream effect.
hazards.detection: Track repeated event IDs, signature timestamps, sources, and effect-key conflicts.
hazards.recovery: Suppress repeated effects, retain delivery evidence, and reverse any effect that escaped dedupe.
hazards.test: Replay one valid payload concurrently several times before the signature expires.

hazards.mechanism: The same provider event ID arrives with a different payload digest, indicating corruption, namespace collision, or provider anomaly.
hazards.evidence: Compare raw digest, provider, endpoint, account, environment, API version, and signing-key version for every delivery.
hazards.control: On event-ID conflict, require digest equality; quarantine mismatches instead of treating them as ordinary duplicates.
hazards.detection: Emit a high-severity alert for one identity with more than one digest.
hazards.recovery: Freeze processing for that identity, retrieve authoritative provider state, and preserve both payloads for investigation.
hazards.test: Deliver two validly signed but different payloads under one event ID and require quarantine.

hazards.mechanism: The provider emits distinct event IDs for the same object transition, so event-ID dedupe alone repeats the effect.
hazards.evidence: Identify provider object, event type, modification/capture/refund ID, and downstream logical operation key.
hazards.control: Deduplicate delivery by event ID and financial effect by a separate semantic key backed by uniqueness.
hazards.detection: Report multiple event IDs mapping to one semantic effect and distinguish this from harmless state observations.
hazards.recovery: Keep both events, suppress the duplicate effect, and reconcile if both already escaped.
hazards.test: Send different event IDs carrying the same capture or refund fact.

hazards.mechanism: Event IDs or object IDs collide across test/live environments, connected accounts, apps, or provider organizations.
hazards.evidence: Inspect livemode/environment, provider account or context, app, endpoint, and merchant identity used in keys and authorization.
hazards.control: Namespace inbox and domain lookups by provider, environment, account/context, endpoint, and event identity.
hazards.detection: Alert on events whose context cannot map to exactly one authorized internal tenant.
hazards.recovery: Quarantine mis-scoped events and audit any cross-tenant state or fulfillment change.
hazards.test: Deliver identical object and event IDs for two connected accounts and for test versus live.

hazards.mechanism: A stale failure, cancellation, or lower version arrives after newer success and overwrites domain state.
hazards.evidence: Record provider version/sequence where available, provider-effective time, current state evidence, and legal transition rules.
hazards.control: Apply guarded transitions or retrieve current provider state; never use receipt time as universal ordering.
hazards.detection: Count stale and illegal transition attempts by provider mapping version.
hazards.recovery: Preserve the stale fact, keep the stronger state, and open reconciliation when facts conflict.
hazards.test: Deliver success before failure and repeat with equal timestamps but different provider versions.

hazards.mechanism: Code treats an event snapshot as current state, or fetches latest state when the historical change itself is required for audit.
hazards.evidence: Classify the provider format as snapshot or thin, its version semantics, and whether the use case needs latest truth or point-in-time evidence.
hazards.control: Choose per effect: fetch current resource for current-state decisions; preserve the event snapshot/change set for audit and causality.
hazards.detection: Log event version, fetch version, and mismatched snapshot/current fields used in decisions.
hazards.recovery: Rebuild projections from the chosen authority and retain both representations with their timestamps.
hazards.test: Change the provider object after event creation but before worker processing and assert the intended semantics.

hazards.mechanism: The endpoint returns 2xx before durable acceptance, then crashes and permanently loses the event.
hazards.evidence: Locate the exact durable commit and provider acknowledgement boundary, including queue durability.
hazards.control: Acknowledge only after authentication and durable inbox acceptance; return retryable failure when storage is unavailable.
hazards.detection: Reconcile provider delivery logs to inbox identities and alert on accepted responses without rows.
hazards.recovery: Request provider replay or backfill by API, then process through the normal inbox path.
hazards.test: Crash immediately before and after inbox commit and verify provider-visible response behavior.

hazards.mechanism: The inbox transaction commits but queue publication fails, leaving an accepted event that no worker sees.
hazards.evidence: Inspect whether readiness is stored atomically, how workers discover rows, and how queue-to-inbox drift is measured.
hazards.control: Treat the inbox as source of truth and use an outbox, CDC, or periodic ready-row sweeper in addition to queue wake-ups.
hazards.detection: Alert on oldest RECEIVED/RETRYABLE age regardless of queue depth.
hazards.recovery: Re-enqueue or directly claim stranded rows without changing their event identity.
hazards.test: Fail queue publication after inbox commit and prove the sweeper still processes the event.

hazards.mechanism: Automatic retries, manual replay, and poison events create a storm that starves new financial events or exhausts downstream APIs.
hazards.evidence: Measure retry horizons, replay permissions, per-event attempts, queue partitions, backpressure, and quarantine policy.
hazards.control: Use bounded exponential retry, per-tenant/provider quotas, poison quarantine, replay audit, and workload isolation.
hazards.detection: Monitor oldest event age, retry amplification, quarantine growth, provider 429s, and new-event latency.
hazards.recovery: Pause the offending replay cohort, drain current events, then resume quarantined items under controlled batches.
hazards.test: Combine provider automatic retry with manual replay of a poison event while fresh events continue.
